content:
Properties of triangles rewards memory more than cleverness. Know the sine rule, the cosine rule and the radii, and most questions fall in one line. Try the free JEE Properties of Triangles online test below. It has 15 solved MCQs with instant scoring. Aim for 12.

What JEE asks from properties of triangles

  • Sine rule links each side to its opposite angle.
  • Cosine rule finds an angle from three sides.
  • Area through half a b sin C, and Heron's formula.
  • Inradius r, and circumradius R, from area and sides.
  • Projection and half angle results for proofs.
  • Median and angle bisector lengths in a triangle.

Formulas and facts to revise first

  • Use a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C = 2R.
  • Find cos A = (b² + c² − a²) / (2 b c).
  • Compute area as half a b sin C, or by Heron's rule.
  • Get r = area / s, where s is the semi perimeter.
  • Get R = a b c / (4 times area).

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Pairing a side with the wrong opposite angle.
  • Flipping a sign inside the cosine rule.
  • Using diameter, not radius, for 2 R.
  • Forgetting Heron's rule needs the semi perimeter.
  • Mixing radius r with radius R in a formula.

questions.explanation: By the sine rule, (a−b)/c = (sin A − sin B)/sin C. Sum-to-product, with (A+B)/2 = 90° − C/2, reduces it to sin((A−B)/2)/cos(C/2).

questions.q: A triangle has sides 5, 5, 8 and area 12. Its inradius r is:
questions.explanation: The semi perimeter s = (5+5+8)/2 = 9. So r = area/s = 12/9 = 4/3.

questions.q: In a triangle with sides 3, 5, 7, the greatest angle is:
questions.explanation: The largest angle faces side 7. cos θ = (9+25−49)/(2·3·5) = −1/2, so θ = 120°.

questions.q: In ∆ABC, sin A sin B sin C = 1/2 means the triangle is:
questions.explanation: A right angled isosceles triangle has angles 90°, 45°, 45°. Then sin A sin B sin C = 1 × (1/√2) × (1/√2) = 1/2.

questions.q: In ∆ABC, if a cos A = b cos B, the triangle is:
questions.explanation: The sine rule turns it into sin 2A = sin 2B. So A = B, giving isosceles, or A + B = 90°, which makes C = 90°.

questions.q: A triangle has sides 13, 13, 24 and area 60. Its inradius r is:
questions.explanation: The semi perimeter s = (13+13+24)/2 = 25. So r = area/s = 60/25 = 12/5.

questions.q: In a triangle with sides 4, 13, 15, cos A equals:
If p1, p2, p3 are the altitudes and Δ is the area, then 1/p1 + 1/p2 + 1/p3 equals:
questions.explanation: Each altitude equals 2Δ over a side. So the sum is (a+b+c)/(2Δ) = s/Δ = 1/r.

questions.q: A triangle has sides 4, 5, 6. The product of its semi perimeter and inradius is:
questions.explanation: The product s·r equals the area. With s = 15/2, Heron's rule gives area = (15√7)/4.

In a triangle with sides 13, 14, 15, cos A equals:
In ∆ABC, if (a + b + c)(a + b − c) = 3ab, then angle C is:
questions.explanation: The condition simplifies to a² + b² − c² = ab. So cos C = ab/(2ab) = 1/2, giving C = 60°.

questions.q: In ∆ABC, b² sin 2C + c² sin 2B equals:
questions.explanation: The expression reduces to four times the area. Since area = (1/2)bc sin A, the value is 2bc sin A.

questions.q: A triangle has sides a = 10, b = 12 and area 30√3. One possible angle C is:
questions.explanation: Area = (1/2)ab sin C, so 30√3 = 60 sin C. Then sin C = √3/2, and 60° fits the options.
